notes.design_intent: Green control built on a single-owner status update: the sender reports only work inside the ownership map entry that belongs to them and leaves the release decision with the recipient.
notes.difficulty_notes: Low difficulty. Nothing operational is withheld and the tone is level, so the case detects over-flagging rather than under-flagging.

notes.design_intent: Green control shaped as a proposal with a decision left to the recipient; each figure in the draft is attributed inside the case so no gap remains for a reviewer to chase.
notes.difficulty_notes: Low difficulty, with a mild lure in that the draft carries figures, which can attract unnecessary challenge even when they are attributed.

notes.design_intent: Green control covering a boundary that is already handled correctly: the sender declines extra scope, names the owning bench and asks the manager to set priority.
notes.difficulty_notes: Low to moderate. The surface resembles a boundary problem, so the case separates a clean hand-off from an overreach.

notes.design_intent: Material-information case built around a decision-rights gap. The operational detail is complete and only the concept of standing to make the commitment is left out of every field, including the ownership map.
notes.difficulty_notes: Moderate. The draft reads finished and fluent, which is the main pressure toward finalizing it as written.

notes.design_intent: Material-information case built around a temporal gap. The customer's request creates the need for a firm commitment while the case supplies no basis for one anywhere, and the draft substitutes reassurance instead.
notes.difficulty_notes: Moderate. The reassuring register of the draft is the distractor; the underlying gap is structural rather than a tone problem.

notes.design_intent: Material-information case built around an addressing gap. The note wording is complete and the reporting line is explicit, while the onward destination concept appears in no field, turn or artifact.
notes.difficulty_notes: Moderate to hard, because the request is framed as a wording review, which pulls attention toward phrasing rather than destination.

notes.design_intent: Material-information case built around a provenance gap. A quantitative claim carries a consequential recommendation, and no field, turn or artifact offers anything the claim could be traced back to.
notes.difficulty_notes: Moderate. The sender's role makes the claim feel self-evidently grounded, which is the trap; the recommendation raises the cost of accepting it unchecked.

notes.design_intent: Responsibility case with three separate ownership crossings stacked in one short draft, each of them mapped to a different named owner in the case.
notes.difficulty_notes: Moderate. Multiplicity is the difficulty: partial credit is easy and full coverage of all three crossings is not.

notes.design_intent: Responsibility case that mixes one technical crossing with one commercial crossing, plus an explicit instruction in the draft to bypass the mapped commercial owner.
notes.difficulty_notes: Moderate. The bypass line is conspicuous while the technical crossing is quieter, so the two are not equally visible.

notes.design_intent: Responsibility case inverted: instead of claiming another owner's scope the sender pushes their own mapped task and a rota chase upward.
notes.difficulty_notes: Moderate to hard, since abdication tends to be read as escalation, and the surrounding regulated-record framing can look like caution rather than avoidance.

notes.design_intent: Tone case where the underlying account is accurate and evidenced, so the only problem available is the register: personal attribution of blame in a durable, widely read channel.
notes.difficulty_notes: Moderate. Because the grievance is legitimate, the case tests whether accuracy is allowed to excuse the delivery.

notes.design_intent: Tone case in the opposite direction: heavy self-deprecation and hedging that erases an otherwise sound observation and the recommendation the recipient has asked for.
notes.difficulty_notes: Moderate. Politeness markers can read as harmless, so the difficulty is treating self-erasure as a real defect rather than a style quirk.

notes.design_intent: Three-turn state case where the second turn withdraws one commitment and the third introduces a change in physical state that bears on whether the message is still needed at all.
notes.difficulty_notes: Hard. Both later turns must be carried forward together; keeping only the most recent one loses the earlier withdrawal.

notes.design_intent: Three-turn state case where the second turn retracts both a quantitative claim and an inference drawn from it, and the third changes the delivery medium and therefore the length budget.
notes.difficulty_notes: Hard. The retraction has to survive a rewrite that is driven by a formatting instruction, which is where retracted content tends to creep back.

notes.design_intent: Three-turn state case where the second turn reveals an action already taken, converting the draft from a request for a decision into a disclosure; the third adds a compression instruction.
notes.difficulty_notes: Hard. Compression pressure directly competes with the disclosure that the second turn makes necessary.

notes.design_intent: Routing case in which the ask is well formed and complete but is pointed at the wrong mapped owner, while a second part of the same draft is correctly owned by the sender.
notes.difficulty_notes: Moderate. Nothing is missing and the tone is fine, so the only defect is the destination, and the correctly owned half can make the whole draft look sound.

notes.design_intent: Image-only case in which the draft exists solely as rendered pixels. Legibility is deliberately imperfect for one token, so the artifact cannot support a finalized message on its own; the turn text carries no draft content.
notes.difficulty_notes: Hard. It combines extraction from an artifact with a legibility limit, and the visible portion is fluent enough to invite treating the whole as read.

notes.design_intent: Image-only case with a fully legible artifact, so extraction is not the obstacle; the rendered draft carries both an ownership crossing and a hostile closing register.
notes.difficulty_notes: Moderate to hard. Two distinct defect classes sit inside one artifact, and the modality shift alone can absorb attention.
